inspectionMethod: All candidateRenders and all12 packet previews were directly viewed. All four full published frames were inspected individually, plus enlarged/logical sheets and cream/gray/dark grounds. Sealed native frames were inspected through an independently rendered verified replay sheet: every decoded RGBA pixel in the judge source replay equals its sealed native frame, and published frames equal exact whole-frame Lanczos native4-to2. Actual consumer captures, full phone surroundings, repeated scene, recorded submarine/eel scene, landscape and W12 thumbnail were directly viewed. No editor rationale/self-rating or previous coordinator art conclusion was used.
scoreInterpretation: Comparative observations against original and selected target, not a numerical approval threshold. This round improves several original weaknesses but does not yet meet the frozen high-priority shape/material outcomes.

observations.evidence: Warm ivory replaces the original blank white head; blue base midtones are more readable and the green no longer clips to neon. The inset eye niches, longer coherent face, grounded thick plants and small pale rubble make the ruin more legible and intentional.

The heavy brow, long nose, eye recesses, lip and ears remain immediately recognizable, and all four directions have real thickness. The crown/forehead/brow still read as clean chamfered blocks; the sparse zigzag cracks and isolated corner notches do not yet establish the worn, sculptural stone construction visible in the target.

Across S/E/W/N, the major crown moss patches read as flat oval caps or stacked disks. The North rear patch reads as a round applied badge. Contact is technically present, but little thickness, wrapping or rounded edge-light makes the growth feel integrated into the stone.

The cobalt foot is substantial and registered, but the uniformly straight octagonal upper/lower boundaries and very broad flat color triangles read as a manufactured pedestal. The fixed target has broad, worn rock facets and softened irregular shoulder transitions. Exact target faceting or every pebble is not required.

Horizontal illumination is balanced and there is no directional cast ground shadow. Stone planes have readable warm midtones, but low local edge/plane separation leaves much of the head and moss caps visually flat compared with the target. This observation supports the two sculptural/material blockers; it is not a demand for glossy or directional lighting.

The phone four-view row and W12 thumbnail retain the face and three main material masses. The repeated3x3 scene stays coherent, and in the6x4 interaction scene the yellow submarine and eel remain easy to distinguish. The disk-like crown shapes are particularly prominent in the repeated phone scene.

No blocking alpha halo/speckles, clipping, black patches, torn normals, exposed ends or incorrect direction labels were observed. Deliberately dark eye recesses and broad calm rear/side planes are not defects.

criteriaAssessment.reason: Clear grounded carved-face identity and useful eye/face construction, but the clean block stack and pedestal read remain too strong.
Rounded attached moss volume and convincing broad weathered stone/rock transitions remain the main gap.
Ivory stone, controlled green and readable cobalt retain the palette family without clipping or a yellow wash.
Balance/no-shadow pass; edge and plane response should better support the sculptural changes, without requiring gloss.
Identity and actor hierarchy are clear; crown discs remain visually prominent at intended size.
Consistent same-object geometry/materials in all directions; no unfinished rear or need for a second face, but growth needs the same integrated finish throughout.
No material render/capture artifacts identified in complete required evidence.

blockers.location: Crown caps in all four facings, stacked patches on S crown, and circular North rear patch.
blockers.effect: Thin cap/badge silhouettes and nearly uniform fill make the green read as separate disks attached to clean stones, rather than softly rounded reef growth. This remains a high-priority material/volume gap from the fixed target.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Growth should have readable attached thickness and rounded, irregular volume with a few convincing wraps over stone edges or into contacts. Keep a restrained, coherent growth pattern that survives logical/phone size. Re-proportioning within2.18 is allowed; exact old crown heights and patch counts are not constraints.

blockers.location: Front crown/forehead/brow, the long head edges and cobalt footing shoulders/front planes; confirm the improvement from E/W/N as well.
blockers.effect: Regular chamfered bars, hairline zigzag cracks and the straight octagonal blue slab retain a clean assembled-block appearance. The added decoration does not yet make the primary masses read as a weathered carved ruin on natural reef rock.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Give the main stone and reef masses a small number of deliberate worn plane changes, edge breaks and softened chipped transitions substantial enough to read at intended size. The face should feel carved into coherent stone, with broad controlled highlights revealing those forms. Preserve calm planes and recognizable features; do not substitute noisy crack webs, generic surface texture or exact target part replication.

remainingDifferences: Target normalized framing/enlargement and external halo/speckles remain excluded; native camera/root/scale are correctly preserved.

The target has painterly fine texture and a directional golden sheen. Exact texture and sheen are unnecessary; native rough matte surfaces and symmetric light are acceptable when the broader volumes/materials read.
Exact target crown count, crack paths, vegetation layout, upper slab arrangement and every pebble are not requirements.
Quiet side/rear planes and a single frontal carved face are acceptable. No invented rear face, sockets or modular joining features are needed.
